summary: Prototype rules passed the historical archive emulator attack cases. Current checkout validation is recorded in verification.md. The rules deliberately deny unsupported direct queries and legacy upload paths; full application compatibility and deployed IAM remain release gates.

findings.issue: The existing frontend performs direct product/user collection queries and first-name profile uploads. The prototype denies these to avoid private profile exposure and ambiguous ownership.
findings.recommendation: Migrate these frontend flows to reviewed API/public projections and UID-scoped uploads, then test the entire app before deploying the replacement rules. Do not reintroduce an allow-all rule.

findings.issue: Server SDK access bypasses Security Rules and actual service-account IAM is unverified.
findings.recommendation: Verify least-privilege runtime and operator identities in the authorised staging project. Never grant clients deletion-job or retained-evidence access.

findings.issue: Rules do not revoke existing download tokens or erase object versions, soft-deleted copies or external exports.
findings.recommendation: Verify the worker's live object cleanup, ownership remediation, approved bucket lifecycle and recovery-copy isolation. Test stale download URLs in staging.
